precepts.text: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: for by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him. So Christ is the firstborn of every creature. By Christ were all things created in heaven and in earth. What is in heaven? All the angels, the host of heaven. Would Satan be a part of that? So who created those evil angels too? So now the creation is trying to tempt the creator. And look at the time that he came: after the forty days of fasting, in a weakened state while in the flesh. He said, oh, I can surely tempt him. This is what he created me to do.
precepts.point: You have to wonder why thoughts start to formulate in your mind that you have not thought about in years. Where does that come from? How do you remember your little girl from the fifth grade when you are fifty-nine years old and do not remember what you had for lunch yesterday? But when the tempter is coming upon you in your weakened state, he remembers everything, and he will whisper that memory into your ear and you will think it is your own thought. A sister gets into an argument with her husband, she wants to cool off, and Satan says, remember him back in the day, with that Studebaker, with the eight-track tape in there. Now you start thinking about him. Satan knows everything about you and him, from back in the day before you even met your husband, before you were even a thought, because you were his employee.
precepts.why:
“Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.” Christ is the firstborn of every single creature, the first created. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.”

By Christ were all things created in heaven and in earth. What is in heaven? All the angels, the host of heaven. Would Satan be a part of that? So who created those evil angels too? Christ did. So in the wilderness the creation is trying to tempt the creator. Think about that.

Satan knew that was the creator. But look at the time he came: “when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.” He came after the forty days of fasting, in a weakened state while in the flesh, and said, oh, I can surely tempt him; this is what he created me to do. Christ answered him with the word: “It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone.”

The same thing applies among brothers and sisters. There is a time when you are in a weak state, spiritually, or physically from surgery or pain, and Satan comes: nobody called to check on you, but here I am; they don't know you like I know you. You argue with your spouse and go for a drive, and guess who is in the passenger seat. He whispers memories you haven't thought of in years, like Cleopus Jenkins back in 73 with that Studebaker and the eight-track tape, and you think it is your own thought. He knows everything about you, from before you met your husband, because you were his employee.

If Satan tried to tempt his own creator, how much more is he going to tempt us? That is why we stay in the spirit and answer him the way Christ did.

precepts.text: And he is the head of the body, the church: that in all things he might have the preeminence. There's only one preeminent, and that's Christ. He's the king; not you, not me. Christ has the preeminence, not Diotrephes. He lost his mind. You know why? He was a hireling.
precepts.point: Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds. Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Diotrephes is another kind of hireling: he “loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.” And the strange thing is, the apostles set this man up. He was always around and made it appear like he was in the truth. But everybody's problem isn't always sex; some brothers want power, preeminence. I was never anything in the world; I'm going to come in and be somebody. Not by the word of God, but by being deceitful and slick and witty, disrespectful in a secretive way.

Paul settles who has the preeminence: “And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.” There is only one preeminent, and that is Christ. He is the king; not you, not me. Christ has the preeminence, not Diotrephes. Diotrephes lost his mind, and you know why? He was a hireling.

We have seen it: a brother in the office of ten sees a congregation in Alaska with no senior man, asks no counsel, pops up, and shazam, he's over the congregation, and because he came from the States they love him and accept him. It happened in Ghana and many of the African countries. Another went out, and where were the congregation's donations? In his personal bank account. You can't make this up. These are hirelings; they don't believe, and there is no fear among them.

Diotrephes was “prating against us with malicious words”: always something smart to say, I know what he knows, I know more precepts than you. He would not receive the brethren, not even the ones that taught him, and cast out any who wanted to visit the apostles. But John says “if I come, I will remember his deeds”, and “Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.”

precepts.text: For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh. Why had they not seen Paul's face? Because he never went to Laodicea and he never went to Colosse.
precepts.point: Which is come unto you, as it is in all the world. On the map, Ephesus is in the middle, Colosse to the right of it, Laodicea above it, and Hierapolis, known as one of the wealthy cities in that region. The word spread throughout those cities. You read about Laodicea in Revelation.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Paul writes “To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse,” just as Ephesians is written to the saints at Ephesus. Same concept: these are Israelites in Asia. Then he says, “Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus.” What is Paul saying? He never went to Colosse. The spirit was so heavy in Ephesus that it spread all throughout Asia, and Paul heard there was another congregation over in Colosse that was fervent in spirit too, so he wrote to them.

Chapter 2 proves it: “For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.” Why had they not seen Paul’s face? Because he never went to Laodicea, and he never went to Colosse. For anyone who wondered why there is no precept in Acts of Paul going to Colosse, that is the precept.

On the map, Ephesus is in the middle, Colosse to the right of it, Laodicea above it (the Laodicea you read about in Revelation), and Hierapolis, known as one of the wealthy cities of that region. The gospel spread through all those cities, “as it is in all the world.” Acts 19 says Paul turned away much people “not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia” from the goddess Diana, the woman all Asia worshipped, just as America worships the Virgin Mary. The spirit was so heavy on the apostle that places he never physically went to were getting touched.

precepts.text: Same concept at Corinth: Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, was practicing the law of sacrifice, but he believed on the Lord with all his house, and many of the Corinthians hearing believed and were baptized. It started with him and then the others took hold of it. Just like a lot of us were practicing Christianity and then believed.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The Colossians learned the truth “of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ.” That is how they woke up: one brother heard it and said, I am going to teach all of you. Acts 18 shows the same concept at Corinth: “After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth.”

“And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house.” If you were in the synagogue, you were practicing the law of sacrifice. Crispus was the chief ruler of it, and he believed on Christ, just like a lot of us were practicing Christianity and then believed. “And many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.” It started with him and then the others took hold of it.

Paul was actually at Corinth, though. With Epaphras it was different: he was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He said, that is true, I believe it, I am going to go teach it. That is just like today when somebody sees IUIC on YouTube, prints out flyers and starts hitting the city, and then this school pops up and that school pops up. We are the continuation of the acts of the apostles, and when we read these scriptures we have to put ourselves in them, because we are doing the exact same thing.

precepts.text: Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, always labouring fervently for you in prayers. I bear him record that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis. Colosse, Laodicea, and Hierapolis are all in that same region. Epaphras was putting in serious work.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Epaphras, the “faithful minister of Christ” the Colossians learned from, comes up again at the end of the letter: “Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.”

“For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.” On the map you see Colosse, then Laodicea and Hierapolis, all in that same region. Epaphras was one of them, and he carried the work through all three cities.

Epaphras was putting in serious work. He heard the truth, believed it, taught it, and kept labouring fervently in prayer for the congregations he raised up, with great zeal for them. He is the example of the brother who takes the truth and gets the ground running in his own region.

precepts.text: There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus. Why is Epaphras mentioned in the epistle to Philemon? Because Philemon was also of Colosse. Demas is named too: remember when you read Timothy, Demas forsook this truth.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
In the epistle to Philemon, Epaphras shows up again: “There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus.” Paul calls Epaphras his fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus. But why is he mentioned in the letter to Philemon? Because Philemon was also of Colosse.

“Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.” Remember Demas: when you read Timothy, Demas forsook this truth. “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.”

The letters Paul wrote from Rome to that region, Ephesians, Colossians and Philemon, overlap and name the same people because he wrote them at the same time and to the same place. Following Epaphras through them shows how the work in Colosse spread from one faithful brother to a whole company of labourers.

precepts.text: Paul writes unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer, and to the church in thy house. It started with Epaphras, then you had others come.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer, And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house.”

Philemon was of Colosse, the same place Epaphras taught. So it started with Epaphras, and then others came: Philemon, a dearly beloved fellow labourer, Apphia, Archippus the fellow soldier, and a church meeting in Philemon’s house.

That is how the truth spreads. One brother, a faithful minister of Christ, wakes up and teaches, and then fellow labourers rise up around him and congregations meet in houses, the same way schools pop up one after another today.

precepts.text: I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds. Why would Paul say that to Philemon? Because they had to be in the same place: Colosse.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds.” Why would Paul write to Philemon on behalf of Onesimus? Because they had to be in the same place: Colosse.

Colossians 4:9 calls Onesimus “a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you,” one of the Colossians. And he is the same Onesimus Paul begot in his bonds and sent back to Philemon.

So the letters tie together. Epaphras, Philemon and Onesimus all belong to Colosse, and the epistles to the Colossians and to Philemon were carried to the same city, to the same congregation of Israelites that had learned the truth of Epaphras.

precepts.text: The salutation by the hand of me Paul. The subscript in many Bibles reads: written from Rome to the Colossians by Tychicus and Onesimus. Some people's Bibles may not have that, so it was posted on the screen.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.” Then the subscript many Bibles carry: “Written from Rome to the Colossians by Tychicus and Onesimus.” Some people’s Bibles may not have that line, so it was put up on the screen for everyone to see.

This epistle was written from Rome, while Paul was under house arrest, which parallels Acts 28, and sent to the church at Colosse by Tychicus and Onesimus. Ephesians, Colossians, Philemon, Philippians, 1 Timothy, Titus and 2 Timothy were written in that same time, which is why they overlap and speak of similar topics and the same people.

Paul never went to Colosse. He wrote to a congregation raised up by Epaphras, and sent the letter by brothers who were themselves of that city.

precepts.text: All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, with Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus, sister's son to Barnabas. If Marcus is Barnabas' sister's son, that makes Marcus his nephew, which is John Mark.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellowservant in the Lord.” Tychicus carried the letter. “With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They shall make known unto you all things which are done here.” Onesimus was one of the Colossians.

“Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus, sister’s son to Barnabas.” If Marcus is Barnabas’ sister’s son, that makes Marcus his nephew: John Mark.

That is the same John Mark that Paul and Barnabas had their dispute over at the end of Acts 15. Barnabas was sticking up for him because he was his nephew. So these closing names are not filler; they tie the letter to the history of the apostles and the men who carried the work.

precepts.text: At the end of Acts 15, Paul and Barnabas had a dispute, and that is who they had the dispute over: John Mark. Barnabas stuck up for him because it was his nephew. It shows you not just anybody can travel. Paul gave him a chance, and when it came to the work he was nowhere to be found. Paul said he is not coming with me any more; Barnabas said, that is my sister's son, I am taking him with me. And the contention was so sharp between them that they departed asunder one from the other.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark. But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.” That is the Marcus of Colossians 4:10, Barnabas’ sister’s son.

“And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus; And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God. And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.”

It shows you not just anybody can travel. Paul gave him a chance, and when it came to the work he was nowhere to be found; he came up missing. Paul said straight, I do not care if that is your nephew, he is not traveling with me any more. Barnabas said, that is my sister’s son, I am taking him with me. You can understand that dynamic. The faithful ministers like Epaphras are the ones who stay with the work.

precepts.text: The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, Galilee of the Gentiles. Zebulun and Naphtali are Israelite tribes of the northern kingdom.
precepts.point: The riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory. The Gentiles here are the northern kingdom, who can come back into the fold. You had no hope unless Christ came and died for us. There was no repentance, no reconciliation, lest it be for Christ.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Colossians speaks of “the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints,” once again using that term saints, and then of “the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles.” There is a Christian out there watching who will say, see, Gentiles means the other nations. Matthew shows who the Gentiles are.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” Zebulun and Naphtali are Israelite tribes of the northern kingdom, and their land is called Galilee of the Gentiles.

So the mystery among the Gentiles is that the northern kingdom can come back into the fold: “which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.” We had no hope unless Christ came and died for us. There was no repentance and no reconciliation, except through Christ.

precepts.text: By revelation he made known unto me the mystery: that the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel. That is the mystery: the animal sacrifice is done away with, and the northern and southern kingdom now have a chance to come back into the fold with Christ. The promises were not made through animal sacrifice but through Christ.
precepts.point: The riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory. The Gentiles here are the northern kingdom, who can come back into the fold. You had no hope unless Christ came and died for us. There was no repentance, no reconciliation, lest it be for Christ.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Ephesians, Colossians and Philemon were written in the same period, around AD 60 to 67 while Paul was under house arrest in Rome, to the same region. That is why they overlap and speak of the same things, like this mystery.

“How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote afore in few words, Whereby, when ye read, ye may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ) Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit; That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel.”

That is the mystery: the animal sacrifice is done away with, no longer in play, and the northern and southern kingdom now have a chance to come back into the fold with Christ. Partakers of his promise, the covenant: the promises were not made through animal sacrifice but through Christ. That is the same “mystery among the Gentiles” of Colossians 1:27, Christ in you, the hope of glory.

precepts.text: He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints, even of the children of Israel. So the saints are the children of Israel.
precepts.point: Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus: every man of the children of Israel. That is what Paul was laboring for; that is why he was getting afflicted.
precepts.why:
Paul calls it “the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints.” The whole question is who those saints are, and the Psalm answers it: “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” The saints are the children of Israel.

A lot of times, when you pull up these key words, it shuts Christians down. They read “saints” and picture everybody who ever went to church. But the scripture defines its own words. The saints are his people, the children of Israel, and the mystery Paul was made a minister of was made manifest to them.

So when Colossians 1:26 says the mystery is now made manifest “to his saints”, it is saying it is made manifest to Israel. That is who Paul was writing to, and that is who the mystery belongs to.

precepts.text: He shall call to the heavens from above: that is the angels. And to the earth: that is the prophets. What is the message to the angels and to the prophets? Gather my saints together unto me, those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice. So when the angels come, they are only gathering the saints; they are not gathering all races on the planet. The angels and the prophets are only looking for Israelites, those that made a covenant with God by sacrifice.
precepts.point: Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus: every man of the children of Israel. That is what Paul was laboring for; that is why he was getting afflicted.
precepts.why:
This follows up on the saints: “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” Read the verse above it and see who is sent to do the gathering: “He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people.”

The heavens from above are the angels. The earth is the prophets. And what is the message to the angels and to the prophets? “Gather my saints together unto me.” So when the angels come, they are only gathering the saints. They are not gathering all races on the planet. They are only gathering the saints, the ones he judges as “his people.”

The angels and the prophets are only looking for Israelites, those that made a covenant with God by sacrifice. That is not all races on the planet. That is not the Philistines. That is not the Ishmaelites. That is not the Moabites. Only Israel.

So the saints that the mystery of Colossians 1:26 is made manifest to are the same saints the angels come to gather: the children of Israel, the people of the covenant.

precepts.text: The land of Zabulon and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles. That is what they called Zabulon and Nephthalim. So the Gentiles that the mystery is regarding is not all races.
precepts.point: Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus: every man of the children of Israel. That is what Paul was laboring for; that is why he was getting afflicted.
precepts.why:
Colossians 1:27 goes on: “To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles.” Now you get to that word Gentiles and they go, ooh, we got you there. No, you ain’t got nobody. Matthew explains the Gentiles.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” Zabulon and Nephthalim are tribes of Israel, and their land is what they called “Galilee of the Gentiles.” Israelites living scattered among the nations were called Gentiles.

So the Gentiles that the mystery is regarding are not all races. When Paul speaks of the riches of the glory of this mystery “among the Gentiles”, he is speaking of Israelites that were called Gentiles, the same people the mystery was made manifest to as saints.

precepts.text: That root of Jesse is Christ; to it shall the Gentiles seek. The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, from Assyria (modern day Turkey), from Egypt, from Pathros (Sudan), from Cush (Ethiopia), from Elam (Persia), from Shinar (Iraq), from Hamath (Syria), and from the islands of the sea. He shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth. So these Gentiles are the remnant of the Lord's people. The envy also of Ephraim shall depart: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. That is dealing with the hatred between our people; if they want salvation, it does not matter how much they do not like each other.
precepts.point: Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus: every man of the children of Israel. That is what Paul was laboring for; that is why he was getting afflicted.
precepts.why:
Here is a follow-up, in case Matthew is not good enough for you. “And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.” That root of Jesse is Christ. To it shall the Gentiles seek. So the subject is Gentiles, and we want to see who these Gentiles are.

“the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.” So these Gentiles are the remnant of the Lord’s people, recovered “from Assyria”, that is modern day Turkey; “and from Egypt, and from Pathros”, that is Sudan; “and from Cush”, Ethiopia; “and from Elam”, Persia; “and from Shinar”, Iraq; “and from Hamath”, Syria; “and from the islands of the sea.”

Then it gets more specific: “he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” These Gentiles are the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah.

Now, you might be saying, but blacks and Latinos don’t get along too much. Read the next verse: “The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” That is dealing with the hatred between our people. If they want salvation, it does not matter how much they don’t like each other in California. God don’t give a damn.

So the “mystery among the Gentiles” in Colossians 1:27 is Christ, the root of Jesse, gathering the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah back together, and ending the envy between them.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart; thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. Love your neighbor as you love yourself, which are the children of your people: that is the children of your race. You have never been taught that in church. We will love any other race before we love each other.
precepts.point: Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus: every man of the children of Israel. That is what Paul was laboring for; that is why he was getting afflicted.
precepts.why:
Isaiah said Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. Here is what that is talking about: “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.”

Love your neighbour as you love yourself, and your neighbour is the children of your people. That word people, children of your people, is the children of your race. You ain’t never been taught that in church. The children of your people is not the Chinese. The children of your people is not the white man. The children of your people are not Arabs.

We have never been taught that. We will love the white man before we love each other. We will love the Chinese and the Arabs before we love each other. We will love any other race first. A Chinese man shot a little black boy in the back and killed him, and he got off, and we are still going to go shop at the Chinese stores, because we prefer other races to our own race, as long as we can get that fake hair, the fake press on nails, the stupid makeup. They said he had a gun; they found no gun. To hell with them. That is why they look at us like we are dummies.

So when Colossians 1:28 says “warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom; that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus”, it is every man of the children of Israel. That is what Paul was labouring for and why he was afflicted: to bring the children of one people back to loving one another and keeping God’s commandments.

precepts.text: We do not cease to pray for you, that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; that ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God. That is how you are not beguiled.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
How do you go about not being beguiled? Paul answered it in the first chapter: “For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding”.

“That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;” “Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness”.

That's how you are not beguiled: filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, increasing in the knowledge of God. If you study, you don't willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Paul said it too: study to show thyself approved, so that you will be able to withstand these men coming in and beguiling you.

The “voluntary humility” of Colossians 2:18 is people giving themselves over willingly. The cure is knowledge. A believer filled with the knowledge of God's will is not left to humble himself to a man with enticing words.

precepts.text: He is before all things, and by him all things consist. And he is the head of the body, the church: that in all things he might have the preeminence. Christ is the head of the body.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.
precepts.why:
Christ is the head of the body. Colossians: “And he is before all things, and by him all things consist. And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.”

Christ is before all things, and by him all things consist; everything holds together in him. He is the head of the body, the church, which is us. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead.

“that in all things he might have the preeminence”. The many members, with their different gifts, administrations and operations, are one body because they all come under one head, and he has the first place in everything. Make sure those precepts are written down: the body of 1 Corinthians 12 is the church, and Christ is its head.

precepts.text: Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints. It was hid for ages that the northern kingdom had a place in this, to repent and come back. The riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles: the secret that was hid for ages is being revealed; it is no longer gatekept. The apostles were going to go throughout the earth and teach the people that you are not Puerto Rican, you are not Dominican, or whatever name was put on them: you are the children of Israel. And that is what is happening to us now in this present time: the understanding of who we are was hid for ages, but the Lord said in this hour the true worshippers are going to wake up.
precepts.point: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they were disconnected from it for so long.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The water Christ gives is “a well of water springing up into everlasting life”, and Paul shows what that understanding is. He is a minister of the gospel “which was preached to every creature which is under heaven”, to fulfil the word of God: “Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints”.

It was hid for ages that the northern kingdom had a part to play in this, to repent and come back. The ones who did understand were the learned men who studied, many of them the Pharisees, which is why they said, will he go to the dispersed among the Gentiles and teach them? They read Isaiah, Ezekiel and Deuteronomy. The masses didn't have the scriptures; the learned men had the parchment. But now he gave it to the apostles to teach.

“To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory”. The riches of this mystery among the Gentiles is that the northern kingdom has an opportunity of repentance: he is gathering back the Gentiles. The secret hid for ages is being revealed to the whole world; it is no longer gatekept. The apostles would go throughout the earth and teach the people that you are not Puerto Rican, you are not Dominican, whatever byword was given to you: you are the children of Israel. “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom”.

That is what is happening to us now. The understanding of this Bible and of who we are was hid for ages, but the Lord said in this hour the true worshippers are going to wake up.

precepts.text: And he is the head of the body, the church. Christ is the head of the church.
precepts.point: The head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God. Paul is not making anything up or creating a list; he went to the divine order that was set forth from the beginning.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
“the head of every man is Christ”. Colossians shows it: “And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead”. Christ is the head of the church.

And Christ himself is under a head: “the head of Christ is God.” Christ said, “The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do”. And, “the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all things that himself doeth”. How could the Father show the Son if the Son was the Father? If you are still stuck on the Trinity, go sit in the corner. It makes no sense for the Most High to show his Son something if they are the same entity.

“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. Here we see order being given, and the headship of the household falls under the same order. “That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father.” To honour the Son is to honour what he said; if you do not honour the order God has given you, you are not honouring the Lord.

Christ said, “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” He is letting us know that he himself is in the divine order and submits to the position he has been given. What do we look like doing anything other than what Christ did?

precepts.text: The day cometh that shall burn as an oven, and all the proud and all that do wickedly shall be stubble. Last time it was water; this time the fire burns the soul and you feel it while you are in it. Pride and wickedness are the fuel, so let whatever you are into go before the fire comes. Sabbath sickness is a slogan for lazy bums.
precepts.point: Brothers who want to give their rank up do not understand the work. The life you used to live died with Christ; now you live his life and do his work. A brother asked how to balance his life: this truth is the balance, and there is no life after it.
precepts.why:
Colossians says, “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom.” Malachi shows how deep that warning really is: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven.” That is why every man and every woman in this truth is warned, and why nobody is played with. Fire is coming for this place. Last time it was water, but the Lord promised that this time it is going to be fire, a fire able to burn the soul, and you feel it while you are in it.

“And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble.” It is their pride and their wickedness that bring the fire on them, so you cannot be prideful. Christ died for your sin; he could have taken you out in that moment, but he gave you grace and mercy. Instead of sitting on your behind, build on the platform of Christ: go out and gather the souls Satan is oppressing, the fatherless and the widow. Brothers who want to give their rank up do not understand the work.

“And the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” Whatever you are into, it is time to let it go before the fire comes. We fight demons every day, and sometimes it is not that you cannot do a thing; you have to command yourself to do it. Sabbath sickness is a whole slogan for brothers that are lazy bums.

So the life you used to live, the wicked life, died with Christ, giving you a chance before the fire. Now you live his life and do his work. A brother asked how to balance his life: this truth is the balance, and there is no life after it. That is the business we are in, in the classroom, on the radio, on TV and in the street: warning people of the destruction to come, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus.

precepts.text: The most High ruleth in the kingdom of men and setteth up over it the basest of men.
precepts.point: The nations are his sword to whip Israel back to repentance.
precepts.why:
Christ is “the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature,” because we have not seen the Most High’s face nor His shape nor heard His voice. The Most High created Christ, and Christ created everything else: “whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.” For him means to do his will, for his glory. The nations are his sword, doing the Lord’s bidding by whipping Israel back to repentance.

Daniel shows who rules those thrones: “This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men.” There are kingdoms of men on every continent, in every country, town and village, but the Most High is ruling them.

“And giveth it to whomsoever he will.” The Lord determines who is that principality, who is that throne, who is that power. Christ is like a chess player moving all the pieces into place so that his will is done.

“And setteth up over it the basest of men”: the lowest of the low. You have to be low down to do what these nations have done to each other and to the nation of Israel. But we transgressed against the Lord, and He said, I have to teach you war. If all the powers were the nicest people on earth, there would be no war and no oppression, and nothing to learn. We have to fight to get back to where we are supposed to be. Brothers and sisters who send messages saying they are taking a break from IUIC are taking a break from the Lord, and that is not going to work.

precepts.text: Surely the Lord will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.
precepts.point: God reveals his secrets to his servants the prophets.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Colossians says Christ is “the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things.” He was the first thing created, before the earth, before the heavens, before the angels. God created him and told him to create everything else: the angels, stars, planets, galaxies and paradise in heaven, and a spiritual realm that cannot be seen.

Moses saw the secrets of that time, creation included, and wrote about it in a similitude, and a lot of it he hid. Those hidden things are the secrets of wisdom, and they are double: a scripture says one thing and also another thing, and when we read it again the Most High takes us to see it on another level.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The secrets Moses hid, God reveals to His servants the prophets. Paul and the apostles understood the depth and width of the knowledge of God, because the spirit of God revealed the hidden mysteries to them. After the last of the apostles’ students died, that understanding died with them and all kinds of paganism came into the church.

But God has sent His sons back on the earth, and the proper understanding of these scriptures is coming back out. People question it when they hear that the men of IUIC are prophets. We are going to show you the secrets, and you judge for yourself.

The fifth angel pours his vial on the seat of the beast, and its kingdom is full of darkness while they gnaw their tongues for pain. The beast is the so-called white man. The place where he rules is the kingdom of darkness, Satan's realm, from which the Father delivers his people. The darkness translates to sin.

The general assembly is the church of the firstborn, written in heaven, with God the judge of all and the spirits of just men made perfect. Christ is the firstborn and head of that church. General assembly explains the word church; it does not identify the Roman Catholic institution as Christ's body.

Moses told the children of Israel that God would raise a prophet from their brethren, whom they must hear. That prophet is Christ, though he is more than a regular prophet. Moses was in the church in the wilderness with the angel speaking on Sinai and the fathers who received the lively oracles to give to us.

The church in the wilderness was the Israelites. The lively oracles are the law given to them. That identifies the general assembly over which Christ is head and rules out the claim that the church here is the Roman Catholic Church.

The command to the married is that the wife not depart from her husband; if she departs, she remains unmarried or is reconciled to him. Reconciled means restored to the friendship or harmony they had before the separation. It is not a new marriage to a stranger.

That ordinary example makes the meaning clear when Paul uses reconcile in Colossians. A previous relationship has to exist before it can be restored. Do not let someone pass over that word and turn Israel's reconciliation into a claim about every race.

The prince here is the priest. His part is to provide the burnt, meat and drink offerings in the feasts, new moons, sabbaths and solemnities of the house of Israel. The sin, meat, burnt and peace offerings make reconciliation for the house of Israel.

Those animal sacrifices restored Israel's relationship with the Father. Paul is now speaking of the sacrifice of Christ and the blood of his cross. The sacrifice changes, but the people being reconciled are still the children of Israel.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: The precept about the mystery of God. “Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints.” “Among the Gentiles”: the northern kingdom of Israel. “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man”: every man of Israel, not Moab, Esau, the Philistines, the Jebusites or Ishmael.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why: “Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints:” The Israelites. “To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you,” So the mystery of the glory, which is Christ in you, had to be taught to the northern kingdom. Why? Because they were lost. They had to be taught the glory of Christ, that Christ came for them to bring them back to the heavenly Father.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

points: As ye also learned of Epaphras, our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ. The church at Colosse heard and learned through Epaphras. That is how they woke up. This brother heard it and said, I am going to teach all of y'all. That is just like today: somebody sees IUIC on the internet, prints out the flyers, starts hitting the city, and then this school pops up and that school pops up. We are the continuation of the acts of the apostles. When we read these scriptures we have to put ourselves in them and envision how the forefathers were, because we are doing the exact same thing.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

points: Paul caught a lot of afflictions for getting this gospel out: who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, for his body's sake, which is the church.
Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints. A lot of times when you pull up these key words, it will shut Christians down.

To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles: now you get to that word Gentiles and they think they have got you. No. These Gentiles are the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah.

Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus: every man of the children of Israel. That is what Paul was laboring for; that is why he was getting afflicted.

Whom we preach, warning every man and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus. Every class is a warning, because destruction is coming; that is the business the camp is in, in the classroom, on the radio, on TV and in the street.
Ask yourself every morning why the Lord chose you out of thousands. He knows where you were and where you are now, and he could have removed you. A soul with no purpose is going to be destroyed.

Brothers who want to give their rank up do not understand the work. The life you used to live died with Christ; now you live his life and do his work. A brother asked how to balance his life: this truth is the balance, and there is no life after it.

God reveals his secrets to his servants the prophets.

points: By him were all things created, visible and invisible, thrones, dominions, principalities and powers, and all of it was created by him and for him.
He is before all things because he is the first formed in heaven and Adam the first man formed on the earth.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

points: That is why he has the preeminence in all things, as the everlasting father of everything, though not his own Father and not the Ancient of days.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

points: The angels gave thanks to the one on the throne; Paul likewise teaches the brothers and sisters in Colosse to give thanks to the Father. He has made us fit to share the inheritance of the saints in light. Giving him thanks is the response to what he has prepared for us.

The power of darkness is Satan's kingdom, Babylon, Rome, the realm in which the white man rules. Darkness is sin. The Father delivers us from that power and translates us into the kingdom of his dear Son. Leaving that darkness means learning and following the light Christ brought.

Redemption and forgiveness come through Christ's blood. Without his sacrifice we can do nothing. Evil is present even when we want to do good; that nature is in every man and woman from the womb. Watch a child take candy when nobody is looking, or strike another child who receives the toy he wanted. The evil nature does not have to be taught, but the light, God's laws, must be taught.

Christ is the image of the invisible God and the firstborn of every creature. Firstborn means exactly that: he is the first of the Father's creations. That is why he is the only begotten Son. He is not merely another prophet. Proverbs explains his existence with the Father before the earth and the rest of creation.

All things in heaven and earth, visible and invisible, thrones, dominions, principalities and powers, were created by Christ and for him. He is before all things and by him they consist. Proverbs 8 and John's opening already explained it. Christ is much more than a regular prophet.

Christ is the head of the body, the church, the beginning and the firstborn from the dead. He has the preeminence in all things, both as the first creation and the firstborn from the dead. The Father was pleased that all fullness should dwell in him.

The church is not the Roman Catholic Church. Church means the general assembly, Israel, the people who were with Moses in the wilderness and received the lively oracles. Christ is the head of that assembly.

Peace is made through the blood of Christ's cross to reconcile all things to himself. Do not run past the word reconcile. It means restore to friendship or harmony: a relationship existed, was lost, and is brought back. It does not mean starting an entirely new relationship with people who never had one.

The reconciliation is of the children of Israel. Under Ezekiel's order, sacrifices reconciled the house of Israel; now Christ's sacrifice does it. If someone claims this means every race, ask when the Jebusites, Philistines, Moabites or Ammonites were in that friendship with the Lord. There is no chapter establishing that former covenant with them. The prior relationship belongs to Israel.

Paul was made a minister by God's dispensation to fulfill the word and reveal the mystery hidden through ages and generations. It is now manifested to the saints, the Israelites. The Gentiles here are the northern kingdom, who must also know the riches of this mystery: Christ in you, the hope of glory.

Christ is the Father's first creation, promised from Genesis, the king of kings and Lord of lords coming through Israel. He is not every race and colour, a Rainbow Coalition; he is of Judah and comes for the nation of Israel. We will rule under him as joint-heirs. The world rejects that mystery. Faith in Christ is necessary to receive the spiritual understanding of the scriptures.
